tagline: Track the relationship, close the deal.
intro: Bond is the CRM where your sales work lives. It tracks the people and companies you sell to, moves deals across a pipeline you shape yourself, and watches every card age so nothing rots unattended. This chapter takes you from an empty board to a working pipeline, a contact with a history, and a deal closed Won or Lost, then shows where an AI agent can drive the same records. By the end you will be able to set up stages, qualify a lead, work the board with swimlanes, and read the forecast.
atAGlance: A drag-and-drop pipeline board with rotting alerts that flag aging deals
Contacts and companies with lifecycle stages, lead scores, and soft delete
Configurable pipelines and stages, custom fields, and org-wide scoring rules
Analytics for weighted forecast, win rate, velocity, and loss reasons
A large MCP catalog, so an agent can work the CRM with a salesperson's reach

pullQuotes.after: moves deals through a configurable pipeline
pullQuotes.text: Shape your own stages, then drag deals across them. The pipeline bends to how your team actually sells.

pullQuotes.after: so an AI agent can do everything a salesperson does in the app
pullQuotes.text: Every contact, deal, and pipeline action is an MCP tool, so an agent can work the board with a salesperson's reach plus the admin config the UI hides.

callouts.after: The default pipeline is selected automatically when you open the board
callouts.text: You will only ever see the empty 'No pipeline selected' screen when the org truly has no pipelines. Once one exists, Bond auto-selects the default (or the first) so the board opens straight onto deals. Mark your main pipeline as default and skip the picker.

callouts.after: It does not collect company, owner, probability, currency, or linked contacts
callouts.text: The board's Create Deal dialog is deliberately minimal: name, optional value, optional close date. Set company, owner, probability, currency, and linked contacts afterward by editing the deal, or supply them up front through the bond_create_deal MCP tool, which an agent can use to collect the fields the dialog omits.

callouts.after: The target absorbs the source's deals, activities, and company links
callouts.text: Merging contacts is one-directional and consolidating: the target keeps the source's deals, activities, and company links, and the source is then soft-deleted. Confirm you have the right target before you merge, and remember the merge loop runs only through MCP tools and the REST API, not an in-app screen.

callouts.after: The card turns orange, and red when it is more than 1.5 times over
callouts.text: Open the Pipeline Board and scan the cards: orange means a deal has passed its stage's rotting threshold, and red means it is more than 1.5 times over. Click a red card, then Log Activity to record a follow-up and re-engage it.

quiz.q: What are the four core objects Bond organizes your sales work around?
What lifecycle stage do new contacts default to?
How is a deal's weighted value computed?
quiz.answer: It is the deal's value multiplied by its probability.

quiz.q: What is the range a contact's lead score is clamped to?
When does a deal card turn red rather than just orange?
choices: When it has no owner assigned
When it has been open for more than 90 days
When it is more than 1.5 times over its stage's rotting threshold
When its probability drops below 25 percent
quiz.answer: When it is more than 1.5 times over its stage's rotting threshold

quiz.q: What are the three stage types a pipeline stage can have?
Which six stages does a new pipeline get seeded with?
choices: Prospect, Qualified, Proposal, Negotiation, Closed Won, and Closed Lost
Lead, MQL, SQL, Opportunity, Customer, and Evangelist
New, Open, Working, Pending, Won, and Lost
Discovery, Demo, Quote, Contract, Won, and Lost
quiz.answer: Prospect, Qualified, Proposal, Negotiation, Closed Won, and Closed Lost

quiz.q: When you close a deal as Won, what does Bond set its probability to, and what happens when you close it as Lost?
quiz.answer: Closing Won sets probability to 100 and moves it to a Won-type stage; closing Lost sets probability to 0, moves it to a Lost-type stage, and records the reason and competitor.

quiz.q: Can members and viewers see every deal and contact in the org?
choices: No, members and viewers see only the deals and contacts they own
Only if an admin grants them access per record
They see all contacts but only their own deals
quiz.answer: No, members and viewers see only the deals and contacts they own
quiz.where: Where to find it: Roles and visibility

quiz.q: When you delete a contact, company, or deal in Bond, is the record erased? How do you bring a contact or company back?
quiz.answer: No, deletes are soft: the record is hidden, not erased. Restore a contact or company by checking Include deleted in its list and clicking Restore on the struck-through row.
quiz.where: Key concepts: Soft delete / Restoring deleted records

quiz.q: How is a bulk contact import driven, since there is no in-app CSV file picker?
choices: By uploading a spreadsheet on the Contacts list
Through the REST API with a JSON contacts array (1 to 5000 records) or an agent, with admin access
By pasting rows into the Create Contact dialog
Through the Bond Settings import wizard
quiz.answer: Through the REST API with a JSON contacts array (1 to 5000 records) or an agent, with admin access

quiz.q: Custom fields are defined per entity type. Are they scoped per pipeline or org-wide?
quiz.answer: They are org-wide for that entity type (Contact, Company, or Deal), not per pipeline.
quiz.where: Key concepts: Custom field / Bond Settings: Custom Fields
